proofs.full_local_argument: Fix N,d>=1 and h,L,R>0; let a=1/(2Nh+1) and choose a unit vector nu in R^d. Define psi(r)=r^2/2 for 0<=r<a and ar-a^2/2 for r>=a. Its derivative min(r,a) is continuous, nonnegative and nondecreasing. Thus psi is convex and nondecreasing. For theta in [0,1], the triangle inequality and scalar convexity give psi(||theta x+(1-theta)y||)<=psi(theta||x||+(1-theta)||y||)<=theta psi(||x||)+(1-theta)psi(||y||). Hence phi1(x)=psi(||x||) is convex. It is C^1, including at 0 and at ||x||=a, with gradient x when ||x||<=a and a x/||x|| otherwise. This gradient is the projection P onto the closed ball of radius a. For p=P(x), <x-p,z-p><=0 for every ||z||<=a: this is trivial for x=p; otherwise x-p is a nonnegative multiple of p and <p,z><=a^2. Apply this inequality with z=P(y)=q, and its counterpart for y,q with z=p. Adding yields ||p-q||^2<=<p-q,x-y><=||p-q||||x-y||, proving P is 1-Lipschitz. Therefore phi1 is convex and 1-smooth, with minimum 0 at 0. Define f1(x)=LR^2 phi1(x/R). Its gradient LR P(x/R) is L-Lipschitz, and f1 is convex with minimizer 0. Start x0=R nu. Set s_i=1-iha. For 0<=i<=N, s_i>=s_N=(Nh+1)/(2Nh+1)>a because Nh>0. Inductively x_i=R s_i nu has gradient LR a nu, so its GM update is R(s_i-ha)nu. Thus the trajectory formula holds through N. Its gap is f1(x_N)=LR^2(a s_N-a^2/2)=LR^2[(Nh+1)/(2Nh+1)^2-1/(2(2Nh+1)^2)]=LR^2/[2(2Nh+1)]. For f2(x)=L||x||^2/2, gradient Lx is globally L-Lipschitz, f2 is convex with minimum 0 at 0, and GM from R nu gives x_i=R(1-h)^i nu. Its gap is LR^2(1-h)^(2N)/2. Both instances have initial distance R and exist in every d>=1. Select f1 if 1/(2Nh+1)>=(1-h)^(2N), otherwise f2. The chosen gap is exactly the stated maximum. This establishes the complete existential claim for the specified algorithm and output, without any lifting to unrestricted algorithms.

assumptions: h is fixed throughout all N updates.

The covered output is x_N; no average or arbitrary transcript-derived output is covered.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean R^d. f:R^d->R is convex, continuously differentiable, and has globally L-Lipschitz gradient. f*=min f. GM uses x_(i+1)=x_i-(h/L)grad f(x_i) for i=0,...,N-1 and outputs x_N.
statement.parameter_domains: L,R,h>0; N,d>=1 integers. No h<2 restriction on this existential claim.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every L>0,R>0, positive integers N,d, and h>0, there exist f and x0 with minimizer x*=0 and ||x0-x*||=R such that the stated equality holds after N deterministic GM updates. No randomness.
